Lessons.Title: Linear Models
ExplanationParagraphs: Learning goal: read a scatter plot, propose and interpret an approximately linear model, explain slope/intercept with units and use the model for interpolation and cautious extrapolation. First-party Edulytiks adaptation of Illustrative Mathematics Algebra 1 First Edition U03:L04, https://im.kendallhunt.com/HS/teachers/1/3/4/preparation.html (CC BY 4.0). The source explores a line of best fit, interpretability and predictive limitations.

Original data for a hypothetical toy-machine test: elapsed hours x=0,1,2,3 and cumulative toy parts y=2,5,8,12. The hand-fit line y=3x+2 predicts 2,5,8,11, leaving a residual of +1 at last observation. Slope≈3 parts/hour and intercept2 already present at time0. The model approximates observations rather than claiming physical certainty.

Interpolate between measured hours: at x=1.5, predicted 3(1.5)+2=6.5 parts, which can describe an expected average output rather than an exact count. Extrapolate at x=5 to predict17 parts, but the model may break when machine performance changes. The line may be reasonable within data but unverified far outside the observed domain.

Student task: plot the four points and a defensible line manually or with actually observed technology, choose a competing line, justify which fits better, interpret slope/intercept and critique an extrapolated claim. Teacher-scored rubric 0–2 each for plot, plausible fit and residuals, correct rate/initial-value meaning and limits of prediction.

KeyConcepts.Title: Scatter plot
KeyConcepts.Definition: Each point represents paired numerical observations.

KeyConcepts.Title: Linear model
KeyConcepts.Definition: A line approximates trends without passing through every observation.
KeyConcepts.Rule: Compare residuals before calling a line reasonable.

KeyConcepts.Title: Interpolation and extrapolation
KeyConcepts.Definition: Interpolation predicts within measured x range; extrapolation beyond it.
KeyConcepts.Example: At x=1.5 model predicts6.5; at x=5 predicts17 but less reliably.

WorkedExamples.Question: Interpret y=3x+2.

Steps: At x=0, y=2, so intercept is two initial parts.
Each +1 hour raises predicted output by3.
Units for slope are parts per hour.
At x=2, predicted y=8, matching data.

WorkedExamples.Question: At x=3 the measured y is12; what is residual?

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Assuming a fit line passes exactly through each observation
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: Real data generally scatter about a trend.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Presenting extrapolated results as guaranteed future facts
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: A trend may change outside measured range.

SummaryPoints: A line can approximate association between two numerical variables.
Slope has output-per-input units; intercept is predicted output at x=0.
Residuals and domain guide reasonableness of the model.
Teacher reviews original scatter plot and explanation.
